text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Slovak foreign ministry has criticised a recent U.S. congress report on NATO enlargement, saying information about Slovakia's lagging in developing democracy and shortcomings in human rights were untrue and damaging the country's image.
- The Economics Ministry said the government was considering unspecified administrative measures to improve the country's trade balance.
- The government holds its regular session on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda does not include any major economic items.

PRAVDA - The government is expected to take a final decision to slove liquidity problems of troubled white goods producer Calex a.s. this week. The paper quotes unnamed sources as saying a foreign strategic investor should be allowed to take a 51 percent stake in the firm.

- Some 521,580 people have signed the petition initiating a referendum on direct presidential elections. The opposition parties said they would hand the petition to President Michal Kovac this week. Kovac then must set the date for the referendum within 30 days.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovak government representatives, led by Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar, will meet with their Ukraine counterparts in Uzhgorod, Ukraine, on Thursday.

- The overall number of cars in Slovakia increased by 120,000, or 231 percent, in 1996 compared with the previous year. Small trucks accounted for seven percent of the entire amount while second hand cars represented 31 percent.

- U.S.-Slovak GSM operator, Eurotel GSM a.s., has signed roaming agreements with Czech and Hungarian operators, and said it would sign 15 more contracts with unspecified European operators by the end of the year.

- More than the minimum 50 percent of Slovaks would have taken part in a referendum on direct presidential elections if it had been held at the end of January. More than the necessary 50 percent of those polled would have voted in favour of the move.
